item.title: Over a million Australians attend church each week - study
item.description: New national data suggests Australia’s churches are continuing a gradual recovery in weekly attendance following the COVID-19 pandemic, while still falling short of levels seen at the turn of the millennium.

item.title: Church community projects linked to falling antisocial behaviour and crime
item.description: A Croydon council estate once known locally for disorder and intimidation has seen markedly better trends in crime and antisocial behaviour over the past decade, with a new study suggesting sustained church-led community projects played a significant role.

item.title: Christians react to US capture of Maduro
item.description: Some Christian leaders have been enthusiastic about US actions in Venezuela, while others have been more cautious.

item.title: I love Jesus, but do I need church?
item.description: Don’t let fear, doubt, or even pride keep you on the sidelines.

item.title: Drone strike on Christmas Day killed Christians in Sudan
item.description: A Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) drone strike on Dec. 25 killed at least 11 Christians on their way to Christmas celebrations in South Kordofan state, Sudan, sources said.

item.title: Concerns Canada may criminalise quoting Scripture
item.description: The Christian Institute has warned that planned changes to hate speech laws in Canada could lead to the criminalisation of quoting Scripture.

item.title: Epiphany: where in the Orient did the wise men come from?
item.description: Many people associate the wise men with Christmas, but January 6 is traditionally the day in the Church calendar that commemorates their visit to the baby Jesus.

item.title: Month-long prayer vigil for the nation gets underway
item.description: A month-long national prayer vigil kicked off this week with an invitation to Christians across the UK to begin 2026 by praying for spiritual renewal, unity and direction for the nation.
